observation: First build satisfied unit tests while failing 3 of 4 ACs at the surface: AC1 (entry path not wired to Conversations.tsx, hidden behind knip.json ignore), AC3 (aggregateToolRun exported but not called by SessionView renderer), AC4 (zero component/DOM tests despite 672-line adapter test suite green). Pattern: 'Green unit tests != green feature.' TDD red/green covers testable units but a feature is not done if unreachable, unrendered, or untested at surface.

Fixture fork anti-pattern: SessionView.stories.tsx delegated to ~1230-line parallel renderer (BareToolRow, HardAggregate, QueuedBubble, StatusGlyph atoms) instead of rendering production SessionView. Fixture became the snapshotted design truth while production component remained untested. Fix: collapsed to data-only by deleting ~904 lines of atoms and having stories render PRODUCTION component fed fixture data.

Design phase reframing (12 rounds, 2 concept reshapes) caught critical architecture assumption missing from AM1: unified message pattern (right-align self + avatars, left-align others). Backporting to shared PartList fixed AM1 conversation parity for free, preventing cascading rework across AM1, AM3, and future message-rendering surfaces. High design cost paid for itself at the source.

Architecture plan item 8 ('update PartList tests for the new avatar/self-box/embed structure') was ambiguous: actual delivery was a separate AM3-session-view.test.tsx file (26 component tests), not updates to PartList tests. Builder may have read this as 'adapter tests sufficient' rather than 'add surface tests.' Plan clarity: explicitly separate 'adapter unit tests' from 'component/DOM tests' as distinct deliverables.

Adapter contract well-defined: 672-line red test suite with exhaustive scenarios (tool_call->tool Part, reasoning, aggregation rules, queued state, composer pills, diff reuse, generic fallback). Red phase correctly enforced source-agnostic boundary (no web imports in adapter). This investment paid off in review when 26 new component tests were added without needing to rework the adapter contract.
